A_trait: floral scent composition across female and male floral phases
decision_note: Primary Annona study characterizes sex-phase scent, pollinating nitidulid beetles and non-pollinating/florivorous/predatory visitor guilds. It is a multi-guild floral-signal source without one common plant reproductive endpoint.

A_trait: flower colour morph and simulated florivory damage state
decision_note: Primary Anemone study measures colour-morph herbivory/florivory, maternal fitness and pollinator response to simulated florivory. Glaphyrid beetles both pollinate red flowers and scratch petals, creating a benefit-cost role boundary rather than fixed opposing-agent geometry.

A_trait: ovary wall thickness; stylar pit depth; floral morphology matched to Epicephala ovipositors
decision_note: Primary leafflower study compares floral traits and pollinating/cheating seed-predatory moth assemblages across 16 populations. It provides geographic coadaptation/trait-matching evidence rather than direct plant-fitness geometry.

A_trait: floral size; mating-system syndrome; pollen limitation and floral parasitism
decision_note: Primary Camissoniopsis study quantifies fruit set across 75 populations, floral parasitism in 41 populations and pollen limitation in focal outcrossing/selfing populations. It belongs to the same biological programme already represented by dissertation source SCHPRISMA-000287 and must not create a new independent canonical programme.
